Station & Tap Crew: Your creatures do their best work standing still. Tapping them crews the Spacecraft that actually win the game, and Sunstar Chaplain turns each tap into value while Dawnsire, Sunstar Dreadnought pays you for a board full of exhausted bodies. Pick this if you like assembling a fleet and launching it all at once.
+1/+1 Counters: An army that gets a little bigger every turn until blocking it stops being an option. Terrasymbiosis turns those counters into cards, Loading Zone doubles them, and Ouroboroid snowballs out of every combat. For players who prefer a board that compounds over a single big swing.
Sacrifice, Void & Aristocrats: Nothing you control is precious here; everything is ammunition. Each death switches on the Void payoffs, so Sothera, the Supervoid and Susurian Voidborn drain, remove and draw off the same sacrifice. Pick this if you want a deck where the opponent can never trade profitably.
Warp -> Void Control: A patient deck that keeps its threats one step outside of time. Warping a spell turns Void on for free, so Alpharael, Stonechosen and Chorale of the Void punish the board without you ever giving anything up. For players who enjoy holding answers and winning on their own schedule.
Tokens (Go-Wide): One creature is never the plan; twenty of them is. Exalted Sunborn doubles everything you make and Moonlit Meditation copies the board outright, until Devastating Onslaught turns the swarm into lethal. Pick this if you love the turn where a pile of small bodies suddenly ends the game.
Lands, Landfall & Landers: Every land you drop is a trigger, and Landers let you drop one whenever you feel like it. Famished Worldsire and Icetill Explorer keep the extra drops coming while Glacier Godmaw makes the whole team lethal out of nowhere. For players who want their mana to double as their engine.
Graveyard Reanimator: Your graveyard is a second hand, and the biggest thing in it is always one card away. Xu-Ifit, Osteoharmonist reanimates with no mana-value cap, so Bygone Colossus arrives far ahead of schedule and Singularity Rupture wraths the board while refilling the yard. Pick this if you would rather mill a monster than cast it.
Second-Spell Spellslinger: Cast two spells in a turn and the deck pays you every single time. Weftwalking makes the first one free, so Cosmogrand Zenith and Sunstar Lightsmith fire on schedule instead of on hope. For players who like sequencing puzzles where the order of your turn is the whole game.
Warp Tempo & ETB Value: Every creature enters twice and you get paid both times. Warp costs let you deploy early and recast later, while Starfield Vocalist doubles each enter-the-battlefield trigger and Cosmogoyf grows off the pile of exiled cards. Pick this if you like a tempo deck that also grinds.
Lifegain & Food: Gaining life is never the point here; it is the currency. Ragost, Deft Gastronaut turns every spent artifact into Food and drains three at a time, while Haliya, Guided by Light converts incidental lifegain into cards. For players who like to stabilise first and win comfortably later.
Self-Mill Sacrifice & Recursion: Fill your graveyard, then treat it as a resource nobody can interact with. Seedship Broodtender mills and then hauls a creature or Spacecraft back out, and Umbral Collar Zealot sacrifices for free as often as you like. Pick this if you want a grindy deck that simply never runs out of material.
Lander Ramp & Trigger Doubling: Make tokens that turn into lands, then make every one of those land drops count twice. Starfield Vocalist doubles each Lander and landfall trigger while Biomechan Engineer and Genemorph Imago convert the extra mana into a board. For players who want a ramp deck with a combo-shaped payoff.
Kavu Landers & Burn: Relentless aggression with a resource engine bolted onto it. Every Kavu that enters exiles a card off the top for Possibility Technician, and Tannuk, Memorial Ensign turns your second land each turn into damage upstairs. Pick this if you want to attack every turn and still never run out of cards.
Big Mana: Skip the middle of the curve and get straight to the payoff. The Eternity Elevator and a pile of Landers assemble seven or more mana, Sledge-Class Seedship cheats the payload in early, and Uthros, Titanic Godcore waits at the very top. For players who want turn five to end the conversation.
Equipment Voltron: One creature, wearing everything you own. Hylderblade hands out the largest buff in the cube and attaches itself on Void turns, while The Dominion Bracelet gets cheaper to move as its carrier grows. Pick this if you enjoy turning a single small body into a threat nobody can answer.
Poison Robots: A quiet alternate win condition hiding in the artifact section. Virulent Silencer gives every nontoken artifact creature two poison counters a hit, and cheap evasive Robots like Interceptor Mechan and Steelswarm Operator get to ten faster than anyone expects. For players who like winning on an axis the table forgot about.
Toughness Matters: Creatures that look like blockers and hit like threats. Tapestry Warden lets your fat-bottomed bodies deal damage equal to their toughness, and Requiem Monolith turns every hit they absorb into fresh cards. Pick this if you like a defence that quietly becomes an offence.
Discard Punisher: Make them throw cards away, then charge them for the privilege. Entropic Battlecruiser takes three life every time an opponent discards and Virus Beetle sets it up the turn it lands. For players who enjoy a narrow, mean angle that attacks the hand instead of the board.
